# Accessibility for Node-Based Visual Editors

Reference file for Dimension 7. All citations reference [citations.md](../citations.md). Updated 2026-04-19: verified [37] W3C keyboard-interface page (corrected to remove unsupported `aria-keyshortcuts` claim), verified [36] Blockly Accessibility Fund (dropped unsupported $5M dollar figure), promoted [34][35] from INACCESSIBLE to PARTIAL via abstract/metadata.

## React Flow Built-In Accessibility

React Flow provides baseline keyboard and screen reader support [5]:

### Keyboard Navigation [5]

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| Tab | Move focus through focusable nodes/edges |
| Enter / Space | Select focused element |
| Escape | Clear selection |
| Arrow keys | Move selected node (when `nodesDraggable` + `nodesFocusable` enabled) |
| Shift + arrows | Faster movement |

Auto-pan via `autoPanOnNodeFocus` brings focused nodes into viewport [5].

### ARIA Implementation [5]

| Feature | Implementation |
|---------|---------------|
| Default role | `role="group"` on nodes/edges |
| Role override | `ariaRole` prop (e.g., 'button', 'listitem') |
| Custom attributes | `domAttributes` prop for aria-roledescription, data-* |
| Live regions | `aria-live="assertive"` for movement announcements |
| Localization | `ariaLabelConfig` prop with node/edge/controls/minimap keys |

### Configuration Props [5]

- `nodesFocusable` (default: true)
- `edgesFocusable` (default: true)
- `disableKeyboardA11y` (default: false) — disables arrow movement, preserves tab focus

## WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7: Dragging Movements

This Level AA success criterion requires that "all functionality that uses a dragging
movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging, unless
dragging is essential" [16].

This applies directly to workflow editors: every node drag, edge connection drag, and
canvas pan must have a non-drag alternative [16]. Examples from the standard [16]:

- Sortable lists: up/down controls alongside drag
- Task boards: popup menus for column transfers
- Sliders: direct track clicks
- Drag-and-drop: menu selection alternatives

Users who benefit include those using trackballs, head pointers, eye-gaze systems, and
speech-controlled mouse emulators [16].

## Four Accessible Drag-and-Drop Patterns

Salesforce UX identifies four major patterns [17]:

| Pattern | Use Case | Mechanism |
|---------|----------|-----------|
| List sorting | Reorder items | Arrow keys + spacebar grab/drop, ARIA listbox [17] |
| Canvas objects | Move/resize on 2D grid | Tab to handles, spacebar grab, arrow keys, grid coordinates [17] |
| Between lists | Kanban-style | Menu pattern with `aria-haspopup`, WAI-ARIA menu [17] |
| One-dimension resize | Column width | Hidden `<input type="range">`, native browser announcements [17] |

Three essentials across all patterns: **Identity** (what is being manipulated),
**Operation** (how to perform the action), **State** (current status/position) [17].

## Production Accessibility Implementation

Synergy Codes built a WCAG 2.1 accessible workflow builder with [15]:

- **Keyboard hotkeys**: WSAD (diagram movement), F2 (editing), Delete/Backspace (removal) [15]
- **Screen readers**: NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver compatibility [15]
- **ARIA metadata**: embedded in every link and transition describing hierarchy shifts,
  status changes, and transitions in real time [15]
- **Visual**: high-contrast color palettes, scalable UI ("zoom without distortion") [15]
- **Navigation**: minimap and dynamic search for large workflows [15]

Note: Specific WCAG conformance level (A, AA, or AAA) not stated [15].

## Visual Programming Accessibility Research

Academic research identifies fundamental barriers [34]:

- Programming IDEs and languages are designed with sighted people in mind [34]
- Visually impaired learners have difficulty understanding overall code structure [34]
- Heavily visual tools impose significant barriers [34]
- Modern programming environments are difficult or impossible with screen readers [34]

Google launched the Blockly Accessibility Fund to support CS-education nonprofits building accessible features for block-based programming [36]. Google's stated 2024 commitment: "adding keyboard controls and screen reader support to improve usability for users with visual and motor disabilities" [36]. Blockly itself moved to the Raspberry Pi Foundation November 10, 2025 [36]. *Note (2026-04-19): prior research claimed a specific $5M dollar figure — that number is not on the fund's documentation page and is dropped.*

The Accessible Blockly prototype (Mountapmbeme, Okafor, Ludi; ASSETS 2022) provides keyboard navigation and screen reader compatibility for block-based programming [35].

## ARIA Best Practices for Interactive Diagrams

The W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide provides authoritative keyboard navigation
patterns for interactive widgets [37]. Key principles (all directly quoted or paraphrased from [37]):

- "For a web page to be accessible, all interactive elements must be operable via the keyboard" [37]
- "The tab and shift + tab keys move focus from one UI component to another while other keys, primarily the arrow keys, move focus inside of components that include multiple focusable elements" [37]
- "The DOM order also determines screen reader reading order. It is essential to keep the keyboard tab sequence and the screen reader reading order aligned, logical, and predictable" [37]
- "Keyboard shortcuts enhance, not replace, standard keyboard access" [37]

*Correction (2026-04-19): prior research attributed specific `aria-keyshortcuts` attribute behavior to this page. The `aria-keyshortcuts` attribute is NOT mentioned on this specific WAI-ARIA APG page; that claim has been removed.*

## The Fundamental Tension

Node-based visual editors face an inherent accessibility tension: the visual spatial
metaphor that makes workflows intuitive for sighted users is inherently inaccessible
to screen reader users. Research suggests "charts/graphs are largely inaccessible" and
"often completely invisible" to screen readers, with table alternatives being the most
reliable accessible pattern [34].

This suggests workflow editors aiming for full accessibility should provide:
1. The visual canvas (primary interface for sighted users)
2. A table/list alternative view (for screen reader users)
3. Code-based definition (the most accessible representation)

Windmill's dual visual + code approach [13] and Retool's graph/tree view toggle [14]
are examples of this multi-representation strategy.

## Gaps and Limitations

- No published WCAG audit reports for any major workflow platform
- React Flow's documentation acknowledges baseline accessibility may be insufficient
  for "apps with more advanced accessibility needs" [5]
- No accessibility testing frameworks designed specifically for node-based editors
- Synergy Codes case study lacks independent verification [15]
- No usage data on how many workflow editor users actually use keyboard navigation
  or screen readers
